name: TPL Plastech Ltd
tagline: Solid ~29% polymer-packaging compounder with parent backing, but unresolved margin quality and no dedicated VP thread keep it short of the 10x/2-3yr bar
business_overview: TPL Plastech manufactures polymer/plastic packaging products (drums, containers, moulded products) and is a subsidiary of listed Time Technoplast. No dedicated ValuePickr thread exists (only the parent's thread); this is a web/news + old-project baseline pass.
fundamentals_narrative: Decent quality: ROCE ~22%, ROE ~16%, a ~29% 5-year profit CAGR, moderating debt (D/E ~0.30) and a strong Q1 FY27 (+37.6% revenue). The old project flagged that independent analyst coverage saw margin erosion beneath the volume growth, with several rating upgrade/downgrade flip-flops signalling genuine uncertainty about margin durability. Parent Time Technoplast provides a stabilising backdrop.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. 52-week range Rs 50-90; stock in the upper portion of its band.
sentiment_summary: No dedicated ValuePickr thread found for TPL Plastech (one rate-limited forum search returned only the parent Time Technoplast thread). Web-only write-up. Old 108-stock project (2026-08-15, frozen) rated it Tier B: 'strong growth headline, genuinely mixed margin picture — watch closely rather than high conviction yet.'
community_signal: No standalone ValuePickr coverage; no trusted-roster signal.
bse_notes: Subsidiary of listed Time Technoplast. Not independently checked this pass.
bull_case: ROCE ~22% and a ~29% 5-year profit CAGR — a genuine compounder track record
Q1 FY27 revenue +37.6% YoY suggests recent acceleration, not deceleration
Listed-parent (Time Technoplast) backing is a governance and operational stabiliser
Debt reduced to a comfortable D/E ~0.30
bear_case: Independent analyst coverage has flagged margin erosion beneath the volume growth; rating flip-flops indicate unsettled conviction
A ~29% profit CAGR, while good, is well short of what a 10x-in-2-3-years outcome needs (~78%/yr)

verdict_headline: Good ~29% compounder with parent backing, but growth rate and unresolved margin quality keep it 'neither' under the open-screen thesis
